title: Matkowski’s conjecture
statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the coefficient field. Matkowski’s conjecture asserts that every two-variable formal power series $M\in\mathbb{K}[[x,y]]$ satisfying the weak associativity equation $M(M(x,y),x)=M(x,M(y,x))$ and having a non-symmetric linear part, meaning $M_1(x,y)\ne M_1(y,x)$, is linear, i.e. has no terms of total degree greater than one.
references: - [On Matkowski’s conjecture for weakly associative formal power series](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00010-026-01320-7) — Aequationes mathematicae — Amr Zakaria

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A 2026 preprint claims the conjecture is false by giving nonlinear continuous solutions, while a new journal paper’s result is not yet known.
progress.summary:
Matkowski’s conjecture concerns continuous solutions of $f(f(-x)+x)=f(-f(x))+f(x)$ and predicts that every solution is linear on each half-line. It arose from Janusz Matkowski’s work on translative, weakly associative operations.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15548)*

**February–September 2026 developments**

- On February 17, 2026, Tibor Kiss’s preprint *A Counterexample to Matkowski’s Conjecture for Quasi Graph-Additive Functions* claimed continuous solutions with nonlinear components, directly refuting the conjecture.
- On April 29, 2026, Kiss’s follow-up preprint claimed broader solution families and characterizations, rather than restoring the conjecture.
- On September 4, 2026, Amr Zakaria’s article *On Matkowski’s conjecture for weakly associative formal power series* was published online, but the retrieved metadata gives no theorem statement, so its effect is unknown.

*[doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00010-026-01320-7)*


Current status (as of September 2026): A counterexample is claimed for the continuous functional-equation formulation but remains unverified, and the September journal article cannot yet be assessed.

*Caveats. The journal contribution may concern a related formal-power-series formulation rather than the exact continuous equation addressed by Kiss.*
